 股價評價基礎： 
AI、半導體帶動用電需求激增，士電已接獲客戶需求，重電 T4 廠產能將於
4Q27 量產 ，2H28 開始貢獻營收 ；2027~2028 進入表後儲能工程認列高峰 ，
預估 2026/2027/2028 稅後 淨利 YoY+29%/+33%/+15% ， 稅 後EPS 
8.10/10.80/12.46 元，給予強力買進評等，目標價 250 元(20x 2028 EPS)，
潛在漲幅 22%。

營運近況摘要： 
士電成立於 1955 年，為台灣老牌變壓器生產商，技術來自三菱重工的技轉，
1H26 產品組合：電力配電(變壓器、配電盤)72%、車輛零件 15%、自動化設
備(工具機)10%、其他 3%。內外銷比 65%：35%。客戶包含：Mitsubishi 
Electric/Mitsuba Electric/ Panasonic/ Hitachi ABB/ Siemens/泓德能源/起
而行/和泰車。目前三個廠區都在新竹：電裝廠、新豐廠及重電廠。

2026 年重電 T1+T2 廠產能利用率提升，T3 廠、表後儲能小幅貢獻 
預估 2026 年營收 415 億元(YoY+12%)，因變壓器需求殷切，重電 T1、T2
廠產能利用率提升至 90%，重電 T3 廠 2025/9 開始量產，Lead time 1~1.5
年，4Q26 開始認列營收，2027 年全面貢獻；且公司在手 500MW 表後儲能
(太陽能儲能)統包案也開始貢獻營收 ； 毛利率21%(YoY+0.2ppts)， 因產品組
合較同期相同； 業外則有 金融資產 公允價值、匯兌利益挹注，稅後淨利
YoY+29%，稅後 EPS 8.15 元。

2027~2028 年 T3、T4 廠產能提升，表後儲能進入認列高峰 
展望 2027~2028 年，重電內銷(佔重電 80%)：政府希望強韌電網計畫完工
期限從 2033 年提早至 2028 年，依 2027 年預算書依然維持 2033 年完工，
2026/2027/2028 資本支出 46/118/155 億元，維持成長態勢。重電外銷(佔
重電 20%)： 為了因應全球 AI、半導體等強勁用電需求，重電 T4 廠將於
2027/9 量產，預期2H28 開始貢獻營收，2029 年全面貢獻，T1+T2 年產能
10GVA(十億伏安)，T3 可貢獻產能 5GVA、T4 再貢獻 5GVA，T4 主要客戶
為日本、美國電力市場，並專注在 345KV 變壓器生產。國內表後儲能(太陽
能)：公司在手 500MW 表後儲能案，若假設 2026/2027/2028 完工比率
10%/40%/50%計算，預計貢獻 7.5/30/37.5 億元，

營收走勢圖

電機機械  
上銀(2049.TT) 
AI 與半導體需求強勁，精密線性傳動元件交期持續拉長

AI 與半導體需求強勁，帶動工具機新一波的景氣循環，上銀生產
的精密線性傳動元件大量用於 AI 與半導體設備 ， 在半導體產業CapEx
確立的情況下，預期這波拉貨潮將延續至明年。在上一波 2021-22 年
的上升循環中，股價最高來到當年度 EPS 的 45 倍，考量到目前僅出
現第一波漲價，研究部以 2027 年 EPS 13.16 元給予 35x 本益比，目
標價為 460 元，給予買進的評等。

1. 半導體設備需求強勁，帶動工具機新一波的景氣循環 
上銀生產的線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿大量應用於 AI 與半導體設備當中，這
波景氣上升循環由從 4Q25 開始，拉貨動能逐季提升。從交期來看，線
性滑軌的交期從去年年底 3 個月，拉長到現在的 4~5 個月；滾珠螺桿
交期從去年年底 4 個月，拉長到現在 5~6 個月。從營收來看，扣除 2
月份有過年因素外 (去年過年在 1 月)，上銀的月營收 YoY 從 3 月的
17.4%一路提升到 8 月的 42.3%，此期間沒有縮小過，顯示營收不但在
成長，成長的動能還在加速。公司亦提到從 6 月開始 BB raio 大於 1，
需求非常強勁，已開始規劃明年過年期間要如何加班生產。研究部看好
這波由 AI 與半導體帶動的工具機需求延續至明年，預估上銀 2026/27
年營收為 300.1/378.2 億元，+23.7%/+26.0% YoY。

2. 市場供不應求，交期持續拉長看好後續漲價機會 
市場供不應求 ， 公司於今年3 月宣布調漲 7~15%， 已於6 月開始反應 。
2Q26 毛利率 34.2%，季增 2.2 個百分點，為稼動率與價格同步提升所
致，預估 3Q26 漲價效應完全反應後毛利率將進一步提升至 35.2%，研
究部預估上銀 2026/27 年的毛利率為 34.3%/35.6%， 分別年增5.5/1.3
個百分點，EPS 為 9.56/13.16 元，+121.7%/+37.6% YoY。 
這波由半導體產業 CapEx 所帶動的景氣上升，研究部看好在交期不斷拉長
的情況下，後續還有漲價、上修毛利率的機會。(上一波 2021-2022 年上升
循環中毛利率最高來到 37-38%)

一、 一、公司介紹 
   上銀科技成立於 1989 年 ， 專注於線性滑軌 、 滾珠螺桿與單軸機器人等精密線性
傳動元件的製造 ， 為該領域的全球領導廠商之一 。 除了持續研發線性傳動產品以外 ，
也自行開發出多種半導體自動化設備 ，產品廣泛應用於汽車 、 半導體 、 醫療 、 國防 、
航太及食品等產業。上銀憑藉自有品牌 「HIWIN」 的深厚研發實力與品質行銷全世
界，目前為全球第二大生產線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿的廠商，第一大為日商 THK 
(6481.T)。1H26 產品營收占比﹔線性滑軌 60%、 滾珠螺桿20%、 工業機器人12%、
其他 8%。2025 年地區營收占比﹔台灣 44%、中國 21%、德國 16%、美國 5%、
日本 4%、其他 10%。(地區營收 2025 年已是最新公布)

圖二、地區營收走勢

二、 產業分析 
上銀主要產品為線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿，產品功能如下﹔ 
1. 線性滑軌﹔一種線性傳動元件，由滑塊與滑軌組成，透過內部的滾珠或滾  
柱循環系統來降低摩擦，讓平台保持平行穩定的直線運動。  
2. 滾珠螺桿﹔一種線性傳動元件，由螺桿、螺帽與鋼珠組成，利用鋼珠在螺桿與
螺帽間循環滾動，將旋轉運動轉換為直線運動。

商業模式 
線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿為工具機零組件 ， 工具機產業商業模式分為以下三種 (以 AOI
檢測設備為例)﹔ 
1. 工具機零組件廠生產線性滑軌 ➨ 工具機 OEM 廠將各零組件組裝成五軸加工
機 ➨ 設備零組件廠用五軸加工機生產高精度定位平台  ➨ 設備商用高精度定位
平台與其他零組件組裝成 AOI 檢測設備。  
2. 工具機零組件廠生產線性滑軌 ➨ 工具機 OEM 廠將各零組件組裝成五軸加工
機 ➨ 設備商用五軸加工機自行生產所需的高精度定位平台或其他零組件。 
3. 工具機零組件廠生產的線性滑軌同時是工具機零組件與設備零組件  ➨ 設備
商直接購買線性滑軌來組裝。

產業趨勢 
JMTBA (日本工具機協會) 每月會將日本所有工具機 OEM 廠的訂單加總 ， 公布 「日
本工具機訂單金額」 ，其產品包含多軸加工機、CNC 車床、滾齒機……等等，由於
日本擁有全球規模前幾大的工具機 OEM 廠，如 DMG、Yamazaki、Okuma，且多
年來產品遍布各個產業所累積的經驗也使得這些公司不論在自研控制器的演算
法，還是機器長時間運轉下維持的精度與溫度都與其他國家有技術上的差距。  
因此，在各行各業景氣轉好，需要大量的工具機時，JMTBA 公布的訂單金額被視
為是工具機產業最重要的觀察指標，工具機 OEM 廠訂單增加 ➨ 增加向工具機
零組件廠的拉貨。 
觀察過去十年日本工具機訂單的走勢，可發現景氣大約呈現兩年上升、兩年下降
的循環。上一次的上升週期為 2021-22 年疫情加上塞港，全球各產業瘋狂拉貨，
使得工具機訂單 YoY 從 2020/11 的-6%，最高拉升到 2021/5 的 142%，一直到
2022/10 訂單 YoY 才轉負 。 塞港造成的恐慌式補庫存為工具機產業帶來20 年來不
曾有過的成長率 ， 也使得隨後各產業去化庫存時 ， 工具機這次的景氣休息得較久 ，
直到 2H25 才再次迎來上升週期。

資料來源：JMTBA

圖七、上銀過去十年股價走勢圖

資料來源：Wind 
（註：與日本工具機訂單 YoY 高度聯動）

而在此波的上升週期，生產線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿等工具機零組件全球市占前二的
廠商，THK、上銀一致提到這一次的需求來自 AI 與半導體，且需求非常強勁。 
細看 AI 與半導體產業，其中涵蓋了相當多工具機的蹤跡，舉凡伺服器散熱所需的
水冷板、快接頭及熱交換器，到伺服器機殼、Compute/GPU Tray 與各種結構件，
都需要以工具機進行切削或沖壓。半導體產業中，在製程升級與產能擴充的過程
需要大量的半導體設備 ，不論在前 、 中 、 後段的設備都須使用線性傳動元件 ， 如蝕
刻機、AOI 檢測設備、各類型 Bonder 等等。 
產品規格方面，AI 與半導體所需的工具機精度更高，使得 THK、上銀這種技術領
先的廠商進一步受惠 。 一般工業用工具機僅需使用H/N 級的線性滑軌與 C5/C7 級
的滾珠螺桿，生產水冷板與快接頭時需使用 SP/P 級的線性滑軌與 C3 級的滾珠螺
桿；在Die Bonder (晶粒鍵合機)與 Flip Chip Bonder (倒裝鍵合機)上則需使用 UP/SP
級的線性滑軌與 C0/C1 級的滾珠螺桿，生產高精度的線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿毛利率
顯著高於精度較低的。

小結 
歷經 2022 年後的全球各產業庫存去化，工具機景氣委靡了接近三年的期間，如
今挾帶著 AI 伺服器與半導體設備需求強勁成長，再次迎來新一波景氣上升循環。
從水冷板、快接頭到各類半導體設備，皆帶動工具機需求快速升溫， 相關廠商也
同步指出需求強勁、訂單持續增加，交期明顯拉長。 
更重要的是，這波需求主要來自半導體設備等高精度應用領域，所需線性滑軌與
滾珠螺桿規格高於一般工業產品，上銀除受惠於工具機景氣重新向上外，亦可進
一步受惠於高規格精密線性傳動元件需求成長。

### Page 9

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 9

三、 三、營運狀況 
1. 1. 半導體設備需求強勁，帶動工具機新一波的景氣循環 
上銀生產的線性滑軌與滾珠螺桿大量應用於半導體設備當中，這波景氣上升循
環由從 4Q25 開始，拉貨動能逐季提升。從交期來看，線性滑軌的交期從去年
年底 3 個月 ，到五月法說會提到 3.5 個月 ， 再到八月份交期已經拉長到 5 個月 ；
滾珠螺桿交期從去年年底 4 個月，到五月法說會的 4.5 個月，再到現在的 6 個
月。從營收來看，扣除 2 月份有過年因素外 (去年過年在 1 月)，上銀的月營收
YoY 從 3 月的 17.4%一路提升到 8 月的 42.3%，此期間沒有縮小過，顯示營收
不但在成長，成長的動能還在加速。公司亦提到從6 月開始 BB raio 大於 1，需
求非常強勁，已開始規劃明 年過年期間要如何加班生產。研究部看好這波半導
體帶動的工具機需求延續至明年 ，預估上銀 2026/27 年營收為 300.1/378.2 億
元，+23.7%/+26.0% YoY。

圖十二、上銀各產品交期

資料來源：統一投顧整理

2. 2. 市場供不應求，交期持續拉長看好後續漲價機會 
市場供不應求，公司於今年 3 月宣布調漲 7~15%，已於 6 月開始反應。2Q26 毛
利率 34.2%，季增 2.2 個百分點，為稼動率與價格同步提升所致，預估 3Q26 漲價
效應完全反應後毛利率將進一步提升至 35.2%，研究部預估上銀 2026/27 年的毛
利率為 34.3%/35.6%，分別年增 5.5/1.3 個百分點 ，EPS 為 9.56/13.16 元，
+121.7%/+37.6% YoY。這波由半導體產業 CapEx 所帶動的景氣上升，研究部看
好在交期不斷拉長的情況下，後續還有漲價、上修毛利率的機會。 (上一波 2021-
2022 年上升循環中毛利率由 31%迅速拉升至 37-38%)

3. 預期景氣將延續至明年，目前評價偏低 
AI 與半導體需求強勁，帶動工具機新一波的景氣循環，上銀生產的精密線性傳動
元件大量用於 AI 與半導體設備，在半導體產業 CapEx 確立的情況下，預期這波
拉貨潮將延續至明年。在上一波 2021-22 年的上升循環中，股價最高來到當年度
EPS 的 45 倍，考量到目前僅出現第一波漲價，研究部以 2027 年 EPS 13.16 元給
予 35x 本益比，目標價為 460 元，給予買進的評等。

本 研 究 報 告 所 載 之 投 資 資 訊， 僅 提 供 客 戶 做 為 一 般 投 資 參 考， 並 非 針 對 特 定 對 象
提 供 專 屬 之 投 資 建 議。 文 中 所 載 資 訊 或 任 何 意 見，不 構 成 任 何 買 賣 有 價 證 券 或 其
他 投 資 標 的 之 要 約、 宣 傳 或 引 誘 等 事 項。 對 於 本 投 資 報 告 所 討 論 或 建 議 之 任 何 證
券 、 投 資 標 的 ， 或 文 中 所 討 論 或 建 議 之 投 資 策 略 ， 投 資 人 應 就 其 是 否 適 合 本 身 財
務 狀 況 與 投 資 條 件， 進 一 步 諮 詢 財 務 顧 問 的 意 見。本 投 資 報 告 之 內 容 取 材 自 據 信
為 可 靠 之 資 料 來 源 ， 但 概 不 以 明 示 或 默 示 的 方 式 ， 對 資 料 之 準 確 性 、 完 整 性 或 正
確 性 作 出 任 何 陳 述 或 保 證。本 投 資 報 告 載 述 意 見 進 行 更 改 與 撤 回 並 不 另 行 通 知。
本 投 資 報 告 並 非（ 且 不 應 解 釋 為 ）在 任 何 司 法 管 轄 區 內 ， 任 何 非 依 法 從 事 證 券 經
紀 或 交 易 之 人 士 或 公 司，為 於 該 管 轄 區 內 從 事 證 券 經 紀 或 交 易 之 遊 說。 本 投 資 報
告 內 容 屬 統 一 投 顧 之 著 作 權 ， 嚴 禁 抄 襲 與 仿 造 。

2606 裕民航運 ( U-MING )

報告日期： 2026 / 09 / 10 研 究 員：林奕頎（ Yichi Lin ） 
壹、投 資 建 議 
一.預期  202 6 年 稅後 EPS + 8.22 元， YoY + 91%，創  18 年新高  
2024 年全年  BDI 平均  1,755  ； 2025 年全年  BDI 平均  1,681 。 
2026 年（截至 9 月 8 日）  BDI 平均  2,5 12： 
1Q / 2026 單季 BDI 平均  1,955； 2Q / 2026 單季 BDI 平均  2,751。 
3Q / 2026 單季（截至 9 月 8 日） BDI 平均  2,9 28。 
2026 年 9 月 8 日 單日  BDI 3,5 84。 運價 強勢，推升航商獲利 。 
二.美伊衝 突日益激烈 ，荷姆斯海峽封閉，油輪運價快速上漲  
裕民 船隊有  3 艘原油油輪  及 1 艘成品油輪 。  美伊 停戰 破局 ： 
原油油輪 運價指數：從 7 月 2 日 1,850 ，漲至 9 月 8 日 2,938 ，
累計漲幅  59%  ； 成品油輪 運價指數：從 7 月 7 日 995，漲至
9 月 8 日 1,702，累計漲幅  71%。 油輪運價 上漲，裕民將受惠。  
三.預期 4Q 是 2026 年單季獲利高峰 ， 稅後EPS + 2.41 元，YoY + 55%  
(1) 美伊衝突， 荷姆斯海峽 封閉 ，天然氣供給中斷 ； 4Q 取暖
旺季，各國 將被迫 以燃煤取代天然氣，推升海運燃煤需求 。 
(2) 聯合國預期 超級聖嬰現象至少將持續到 2027 年 2 月，極端
氣候橫行 ； 巴拿馬運河缺水 嚴峻，持續降低船舶通行量，
將壓抑海運供給 。  即使超級聖嬰解除；  依過去 5 年資料
（參閱圖 1）， 巴拿馬運河季節性乾季最低水位會落在 5 月。 
(3) 散裝航運以  4Q 為例行的季節性 旺季 。 
基於 (1) ~ (3) ，宏遠預期 4Q 將是裕民  2026 年單季獲利高峰。  
四.基於保守，估 2027 年 BDI 僅 2,490 ，裕民稅後 EPS + 7.10 元 
2026 年 9 月 8 日 單日  BDI 指數  3,5 84。 
宏遠 基於保守 原則，假設  三大利空在 2027 年落實 ： 
(1) 荷姆斯 海峽不再受阻 ，天然氣供給上升，壓抑煤炭需求 。 
(2) 超級 聖嬰解 除，巴拿馬運河不再缺水。  
(3) 全球散裝 船舶 下水量大增 。 
宏遠 估 2027 年 BDI 平均值僅  2,490； 裕民稅後 EPS + 7.10 元。 
若上述三項利空沒有落實，則必須調高裕民  2027 年獲利預估 。 
五.建議： 4Q 旺季  遇上  戰爭及聖嬰；  估 2026 年獲利，18 年新高  
2026 年截至 9 月 8 日，BDI 指數都 大幅 高於 2025 年同期（參閱
圖 2）； 此外，美伊戰爭造成 荷姆斯海峽中斷 ，須以燃煤取代
天然氣，推升散裝海運需求；  而 超級聖嬰 帶來全球乾旱，即

貳、公 司 概 況 
一.公司簡介  
截至 2026 年 5 月（法說資料），裕民實際經營船隻為 71 艘：  
海岬型船   25 艘：自有 22 艘 + 3 艘合資。  
巴拿馬型船 24 艘：自有 14 艘 + 7 艘代管  + 3 艘合資 。 
輕便型      8 艘（自有） 。 
水泥船      4 艘（自有） 。 
油輪        4 艘：透過  環能海運 （持股 40% ）。 
CTV 離岸風電人員運輸船 6 艘（自有  ； 裕民風能航運 ）。

在建船隻  12 艘，交船時程 ： 
202 6 年： 輕便型  1 艘（預期 11 月交付）。 
202 7 年 及 2028 年： 
海岬型  4 艘 + 輕便型  5 艘 + 風電工程船  2 艘。

二.營運概況 及展望  
1.超級聖嬰 造成缺水  撞上  巴拿馬運河乾季，壓抑海運供給  
2026 年 5 月，全球進入聖嬰年，加劇全球乾旱與極端高溫 的
氣候異常 。 聯合國  世界氣象組織（ WMO ）表示， 這波聖嬰
現象，可能是過去  40 年最強一次，幾乎肯定會持續到  2027
年 2 月，很可能打破  2023 年 ~ 2024 年的紀錄 。

巴拿馬運河溝通大西洋與太平洋，節省海運船舶至少  3,000
海哩的航程，航行時間縮短  2 週左右。

但由於 大西洋與太平洋的海平面和水流高度不同，船隻 要透
過 巴 拿 馬 運 河 ，橫 跨 美 洲 ， 必 須依 靠 巴 拿 馬 運 河 的船閘 注
水，採取類似 爬樓梯一樣 的升降 動作 ，讓船 隻從海平面被提
升到高處的加通湖，穿過湖面後，再降回另一側的海平面。
每艘船舶 每次通過船閘，都需要消耗  加通湖  數以百萬加侖
計算的淡水。

因此， 加通湖的水量多寡 ，會影響巴拿馬運河的運作效率與
容量 ，一旦缺水，巴拿馬運河每日通行船舶數量就會減少。

觀察過去 5 年（2021 年 ~ 2025 年）加通湖的水位資料（參閱
圖 1） ，通常會從每年 5 月，逐月爬升到  12 月；  但 2026 年
超級聖嬰的乾旱，造成目前 9 月水位不升反降 。 
以現貨為主，長約為輔 
總船隊 71 艘 
全球 超級聖嬰 極端氣候 
從 2026 年 5 月 至少持續 
至 2027 年 2 月

巴拿美運河 季節性乾季 從 
每年 12 月 持續至 隔年 5 月

聖嬰 + 乾季 
預期巴拿馬運河 要解除缺水 
最快必須等到 2027 年 2H

2026 年 5 月起，全球 超級聖嬰 ，帶來的 乾旱，至少將持續到
2027 年 2 月 ； 如此，將撞上  加通湖  每年  例行 的 季節 性 
乾季 （每年 12 月 ~ 隔年 5 月 ； 參閱圖 1 ）。

因此， 巴拿馬運河（ 加通湖）的缺水很可能會持續加重，最
快的解除時間可能要等到  2027 年 2H。

巴拿馬運河  每日正常通行量  36 ~ 40 艘。 
2023 年 ~ 2024 年 全球 聖嬰 造成乾旱  巴拿馬運河的 每日船
舶通行量最低降至  18 艘。

目前  加通湖  尚未進入  季節性乾季，但 受制於全球聖嬰現
象， 加通湖  水位  已經 提前 明顯降低 ； 巴拿馬運河管理當
局， 已經 宣布，巴拿馬運河每日船舶通行數量， 2026 年 9 月
3 日降至  34 艘 ； 9 月 15 日降至  32 艘。

宏遠預期， 巴拿馬運河降低每日船舶通行數量的趨勢，將日
益嚴重， 壓抑所有的海運供給 ，將有利於推升各型船舶的運
價，拉高海運航商獲利 。

圖 1：加通湖 過去 5 年 每月平均水位變化 ； 5 月 走升至 12 月（雨季） ； 12 月 再走跌至 5 月（乾季） 
超級聖嬰帶來乾旱，造成 2026 年 9 月水位 不升反降 。

2.散裝 BDI 走勢，隱示  2026 年獲利  將大幅優於  2025 年 
2026 年截至 9 月 8 日，散裝 BDI 運價走勢都優於 2025 年同期
表現（ 參閱圖 2） 。 
受惠於 BDI 的強勁走勢 ，裕民 ： 
1Q / 2026 稅後 EPS + 1.17 元，優於  1Q / 2025 同期  + 0.27 元。 
2Q / 2026 稅後 EPS + 2.34 元，優於  2Q / 2025 同期  + 0.77 元。

從 BDI 的表現來看：  
1Q / 2026 （過年淡季） BDI 平均  1,955 。 
2Q / 2026 （美伊戰爭爆發， 燃煤替代天然氣） BDI 平均  2,751 。 
3Q / 2026 （截至 9 月 8 日） BDI 平均  2,928。 
2026 年 9 月 8 日 單日  BDI  3,584 。

4Q 是散裝 航運的 季節性 旺季，遇上， 荷姆斯海峽封閉  推升  
煤 炭 的 海 運 需 求  及   巴 拿 馬 運 河 缺 水 降低  海運船舶供
給（繞道等同減少供給） ； 預期 4Q 的 BDI 將會持續強勁。

BDI 漲勢 強勁，宏遠預期 裕民  3Q ~ 4Q / 2026 單季獲利 YoY 大
幅成長 ； 未來， 3Q 及 4Q 財報發布 ，將激勵股價表現 。

Valuation
Our target price for EMC is set at NT$6,000, based on a target PE multiple of 30x on our 2027E EPS average. We believe our
target PE multiple, at the peak of its forward PE average in the past 5 years, is justified by a strong earnings outlook supported
by its leading position in CCL supply for AI GPU and ASIC (high m/s) from 2026E onwards. We also believe the continued spec

upgrade for CCL and price hikes should help support its margin expansion going forward. At our target price, the shares would
trade at 23.6x/13.2x 2026E/27E PB.
Risks
Citi’s quant system rates EMC high-risk given high share price volatility, which we largely attribute to frequent debates over the
spec upgrade for next-gen AI servers. In general, we believe some investors initially tend to have high hope for aggressive spec
upgrade without sufficiently considering the scalability and cost structure of CCL products, which then leads to a shortfall in

the end. However, from a longer-term perspective, we see a decent and clear spec upgrade trend with meaningful ASP growth
potential among AI servers of different generations. As such, we do not assign a high-risk rating.
Key downside risks that could prevent the shares from reaching our target price include: 1) a slower-than-expected CCL
upgrade trend; 2) weaker-than-expected AI server demand; 3) production bottlenecks in AI supply chain (eg, glass, copper foil,

foundry or OSAT); 4) unexpected share loss in key AI server projects; and 5) stricter practice of OOC policy by end customers.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.
Catalyst Watch/Short Term Views (“STV”) Ratings Disclosure:

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi Research may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside
call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in
reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be
published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is

moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day
period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds
15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV
call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be

In this report, we focus on King Slide's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price movement.
Details:
• August sales were NT$6,466mn (+1% MoM/+344% YoY) – another record
high.
• QTD revenue reached 66% of MSe, at NT$19,555mn (+81% QoQ/+348%
YoY), and 77% of consensus, at NT$16,755mn (+55% QoQ/+284% YoY).
Our view:
• We see 3Q26 revenue tracking in line with our estimate.

• On top of the mainstream GPU/ASIC server demand from hyperscalers, we
believe that King Slide is generating more revenue from various projects in
different applications as well.
• We believe the company should continue to benefit from server market
growth and increasing dollar content, driven by more complex designs and
broader adoption of rail kits. We view it as a good proxy for the AI capex
cycle, given its dominant position, strong patent portfolio, and solid

execution.
• Stay OW.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
King Slide Works Co. Ltd. (2059.TW)
Base case, 30x 2027e P/E. We use price/earnings as our valuation methodology because we
believe it better captures King Slide's earnings growth potential. We believe our target mul-
tiple is justified by an operating profit CAGR of 77% seen for 2025-28, implying a PEG of 0.4
vs. the average of 1.2 over 2010-24, when the stock was trading at 17-18x P/E with an operating

profit CAGR of 14%.
Risks to Upside
n Stronger-than-expected AI capex
n Stronger server demand
n Faster market share gains
Risks to Downside
n Softer AI capex
n Weaker server demand
n Sluggish kitchen furniture demand
n Competition leading to slower share gains.

Analyst Stock Ratings
Overweight (O). The stock's total return is expected to exceed the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk -adjusted basis, over the next
12-18 months.
Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk -adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk -adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk -adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.

Yageo
Valuation
We set our target price at NT$1,450, based on 35x average 2027E-28E earnings. We value Yageo based on PE as we believe the
company’s earnings performance and industry dynamics would be the key focuses of the market. Our target multiple of 35x is
at the higher end of the trading range since 2022. During this period the company has gone through the cycles, successfully
integrated the acquired business to enhance its product offerings, and started to deliver stable margins and earnings.

Risks
Key downside risks to our target price and rating include: 1) slower-than-expected demand recovery; 2) intensified peer and
pricing competition; 3) execution risks associated with M&A integration and synergies; and 4) FX and interest rate fluctuations.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi Research may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside
call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in
reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be
published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is

moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day
period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds
15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV
call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be

our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do

## Document 095: 260908_gs_semicon-TW

### Page 1

1. Photonics IC scaling up: AI drives data transmission speed and bandwidth 
requirement, leading to strong demand on Photonics IC, requesting it to catch up 
Electrical IC automated production and testing ecosystem in 1 to 2 years, while EIC / 
semiconductors has been developed for decades. The strong demand brings 
opportunities to tool suppliers, across coupling and testing, which are necessary 
tools to accelerate PIC production. Robotechnik / FiconTEC describes the numbers of 
tools they target to ship in coming 1 year would be over 50% of what they’ve shipped 
in past 25 years, reflecting the strong demand and orders visibility.  
2. Testing - CPO earliest beneficiary: As a new technology, CPO naturally takes time 
and faces challenges in the path of commercialization; however, we identify testing 
equipment suppliers as the earliest beneficiaries, considering the expensive final 
module means multiple testing during the production process is necessary, given the 
earlier a failure is found, the lower cost a failure is. As a result, companies we visited 
continue to see Insertion 2 (double sided wafer-level testing) as necessary, and 
Robotechnik / FiconTEC launched the new generation in 3Q26, which fully complied 
with the global leading foundry’s communication infrastructure. 
3. Testing - shortening time with KGD (know good die) at early stage: To facilitate 
photonics IC scaling up, not only are more tools needed but better tools, requiring 
suppliers’ strong R&D and execution, delivering continuous specification upgrade. 
Robotechnik / FiconTEC, as global leaders in PIC testing, aim to shorten the 
wafer-level testing time by 50-60% next year, and target 4x faster die-level testing 
next year. Enlitech (7728.TWO, Not Covered) offers NightJar, a hyperspectral image 
system, revealing AWG (arrayed waveguide grating) optical loss pathways with 
absolute optical power mapping, allowing customers to KGD at Insertion 1 (PIC wafer

### Page 2

testing) or Insertion 0 (PIC wafer early defect screening), saving failure costs. 
4. Coupling - automated production becoming necessary in high-speed connection: 
AI drives optical module towards high speed and high density / bandwidth, driving 
demand on automated production. GMT (4573.TWO, Not Covered) showcased dual FA 
active alignment equipment for 1.6T optical module, which could do the coupling for 
both Tx and Rx simultaneously, saving 50% of coupling time compared to traditional 
equipment. FitTech (6706.TW, Not Covered) showcased optical engine assembly system, 
featuring with passive / active alignment and customized development of coupling 
algorithms, which could be used in multiple products: high-speed optical modules, ELS, 
OCS, NPO, CPO, SiPh and optical chiplets. ASMPT showcased MEGA multi-chip bonding 
solution for complex multi-chip and photonics packaging applications, combining 
high-precision placement with adhesive dispensing, UV fixation and 3D inspection in one 
platform. 
5. FAU & Laser specification upgrade: With optical networking expanding from scale 
out to scale up, FAU and laser specification is also migrating. We estimate FOCI‘s FAU in 
2026E to be mainly 40 channels (starting in 3Q26) for 3.2T, followed by 80 channels 
(within 2026E) for 6.4T, and 100 channels under R&D. The company’s FAU enjoys several 
customers across fabless, foundry, laser suppliers, etc. FOCI Aug revenues accelerated to 
+20% MoM (vs. +9% MoM in Jul), reflecting the ramp up of high-end FAU. VPEC‘s 
optoelectronics revenues enjoy strong growth on the back of strong CW lasers demand 
and InP substrate supply getting better. Its InP epiwafer for CW lasers is also migrating 
from 70mW / 100mW (scale out) to above 100mW (scale up, NPO) and 300mW / 
400mW (scale up, CPO), along with expansion from CW lasers to 100G / 200G EML, 
supporting its growth ahead. 
6. AI drives CMP slurry: Anji Micro owns a comprehensive customer base, allowing it to 
ride on growing AI spending across China and overseas. The global-tier AI infrastructure 
continues to migrate, driving the CMP slurry consumption per system, along with AI 
server racks ramp up, enlarging the total addressable market. As the CMP slurry local 
leader, we are positive on Anji’s capability to offer qualified and reliable semi material 
products to penetrate global-tier clients.

Price target methodology and risks - ASMPT
Valuation methodology: We are Neutral-rated on ASMPT with a 12-month target price
of HK$177, which is based on 24.9x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E).
Our target P/E is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and
OPM.
Key upside/downside risks: 1) customers’ faster-/slower-than-expected adoption of
Advanced Packaging tools; 2) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand from

automotive customers; and 3) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand for traditional
IC packaging and SMT equipment.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - Anji Micro
Valuation: We are Buy-rated on Anji Micro with a 12-month target price of Rmb509,
which is based on 46x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E). Our target P/E
is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and OPM.
Key downside risks: 1) supply chain risks; 2) weaker semi client demand; and 3)

weaker-than-expected product expansion.
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of NT$833 is based on a 15.4x 2030E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 12.6%. Our target multiple is derived from peers’
correlation between forward-year trading P/E and earnings growth.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition, technology migration
trends in optical networking, and slower-than-expected capacity ramp-up.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - VPEC

Valuation: We adopt a discounted P/E method and apply a 22.2x target P/E on VPEC’s
2029E EPS, discounting back to 2027E at a COE of 10.5% (beta 1.7x, risk free rate 1.6%
and market risk premium at 5.1%), to derive our 12m TP of NT$793. Our target P/E is
based on a 0.4x PEG&M ratio derived from the average level of peers in the photonics
supply chain.
Key risk: Slower-than-expected SiPh business ramp up; weaker-than-expected
microelectronics demand from smartphones clients; IDM offers EPI wafer in-house.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - RoboTechnik
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of Rmb796 is based on a 20.7x 2031E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 11.3%. Our target multiple is derived from the
correlation between consumer electronic peers’ PEG&M (2026E P/E to 2027E NI YoY and
OPM), with RoboTechnik’s 2032E net income at 2% YoY and 2032E OPM at 32%.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition; lower-than-expected

optical connection end demand; worse-than-expected photovoltaic market downcycle.

Summary: Driven by strong AI/HPC demand, all three companies set new revenue 
milestones: Winway (TWD 1.71bn, +6.6% MoM, +233.4% YoY), MPI (TWD 2.05bn, 
+13.4% MoM, +69.9% YoY), and CHPT (TWD 638m, +3.9% MoM, +54.3% YoY). With 
Winway’s capacity expansions tracking ahead of schedule, MPI set to begin shipping CPO 
insertion 3 products in 4Q26 alongside ASP hikes in late-3Q26, and CHPT nearing a 
qualification for its turnkey CPU ASIC project, the sector offers resilient sequential growth 
visibility through 2H26 and potential earnings upside heading into 2027.

What’s new: Following the conclusion of SEMICON Taiwan, we have observed a marked 
uptick in investor enquiries regarding the semiconductor test interface supply chain. As 
AI/HPC architectural transitions, and the increasing complexity of 2.5D/3D packaging drive 
structural content gains, investors have focused increasingly on capacity visibility and 
technological roadmaps across the socket and probe card segments. In the note, we recap 
the latest August monthly revenue figures and synthesize key market dynamics across our 
coverage universe.

WinWay Technology (6515 TT, TWD7,280, Buy [1]) 
• Aug revenue result: Monthly revenue reached TWD 1.71bn ( +6.6% MoM, +233.4% 
YoY), bringing 1-8M26 cumulative revenue to TWD 9.81bn (+97.9% YoY). Jul-Aug sales 
reached 72% of our 3Q26E revenue, tracking ahead of our expectations.

• Product mix & catalysts: Growth remains anchored by aggressive tape-outs from 
North American GPU leaders and cloud hyperscalers. Shipments of proprietary coaxial 
test sockets and advanced wafer-level vertical probe cards expanded sharply. While the 
market may expect meaningful revenue contributions from CPO sockets or probe cards, 
we believe it will account for mid-single digit in 2027E and high-single digit in 2028E.

• Outlook: The company maintained a constructive stance on order visibility and 
persistent demand-supply tightness. Management reaffirmed that 2Q26 marked the 
near-term cyclical trough, guiding for sequential revenue expansion on a QoQ basis 
moving forward. Our supply chain checks indicate that capacity expansion execution is 
tracking ahead of schedule compared with last month. With Winway poised to bring 
additional capacity online in 2027, we suggest investors monitor the company’s 2H26 
earnings call (mid-Nov) for further clarity on its 2027 capex and capacity roadmap.

• Valuation: We have a Buy (1) rating with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a 
target PER of 70x applied to our 4-quarter-forward EPS forecast. Based on our 
2027/28E EPS, the stock is currently trading at PERs of 36.9x/19.5x, vs. its previous 
highs of 80-90x. Downside risks: heavy reliance on major US AI chipmakers and; 2) 
intensifying competition that could erode design wins.

MPI Corporation (6223 TT, TWD5,615, Buy[1]) 
• Aug revenue result: Monthly revenue surpassed the TWD 2bn milestone for the first 
time, reaching TWD 2.05bn (+13.4% MoM, +69.9% YoY), bringing 1-8M26 cumulative 
revenue above TWD 13.0bn. Jul-Aug sales reached 63% of our 3Q26E revenue 
estimate, tracking slightly below our expectations.

2
•2027 Pricing Looks More Favorable.  Management hopes to implement broader-based price increases across AI and
non-AI products to offset higher wafer, energy and other input costs and support new capacity investments. Pricing
should therefore turn more positive in 2027 if utilization remains high. Management noted that every 1% ASP
increase could improve gross margin by roughly 0.5–0.6ppt. However, margins are unlikely to revisit the >45%

COVID-era peak because depreciation is structurally higher following the current investment cycle.
•Intel 12nm cooperation: Capital-Light Path, contribution starting in late 2027 . The Intel collaboration is
strategically important because it gives UMC a capital-light path from its strong 22/28nm franchise into 12nm. Intel
provides existing Arizona manufacturing equipment and capacity, while UMC contributes technology conversion, RD
resources and its existing customer relationships. Initial customers are primarily Wi-Fi and communications-related,

with the first meaningful revenue expected around late 2027; broader contribution should build gradually thereafter
as customers validate the first wave. UMC expects to book the wafer revenue, with Intel manufacturing costs flowing
through UMC’s cost structure and economics broadly shared between the two parties. Expansion into smaller nodes
or advanced packaging with Intel remains possible, but management stressed that 12nm must first demonstrate

competitive yield, manufacturing performance and profitability.
•Silicon Photonics: Singapore Fab Becomes a Major AI Growth Platform.  The company is building dedicated 12-inch
capacity for silicon photonics in Singapore, with the new facility expected to be ready in roughly 14 months.  The
platform can encompass PICs and related components such as TIA, with management describing demand as
stronger than its available engineering resources.  UMC also has exposure to TFLN through an affiliate focused

initially on 6-inch technology, with potential migration to 8-inch manufacturing supported by UMC. Current
economics are attractive because photonics wafers can command multiples of conventional CMOS wafer pricing.
Longer term, UMC wants to combine silicon photonics, specialty materials and packaging capabilities into an
integrated platform.
•Advanced Packaging: Building an Open-Ecosystem Second Source. Advanced packaging represents UMC’s third
major structural growth driver. Rather than competing directly with TSMC’s fully integrated leading-edge ecosystem,

UMC aims to become a credible second-source, open-ecosystem provider. Its developing capabilities include
interposers, wafer-to-wafer and hybrid bonding, DTC, and related packaging processes, with silicon photonics
potentially integrated into the same broader solution. UMC is constructing two new advanced-packaging facilities in
Taiwan. Construction is expected to take more than two years, while existing facilities can provide limited capacity
during the interim.

•Specialty Strategy Provides Defense Against China Competition. UMC continues to differentiate itself through
specialty technologies rather than competing primarily on commodity mature-node capacity. Management
estimates 50–60%+ of revenue now comes from specialty processes, which provides meaningful insulation from
Chinese foundry pricing pressure. China’s semiconductor market is also becoming increasingly segmented into
“China-for-China” and “non-China-for-non-China” supply chains, limiting direct cross-border price competition.

UMC’s two China fabs remain highly utilized and represent roughly 10% of group capacity. Overall, UMC’s strategy is
shifting from being primarily a mature-node foundry toward a specialty and heterogeneous-integration platform
while improving utilization and pricing provide a stronger cyclical backdrop for 2027.

UMC
Valuation
Our target price for UMC of NT$125 is based on 15x 2027E EPS, which is higher than the midpoint of its 3-year forward PE. We
believe our target multiple is justified by our belief that UMC should benefit from the robust demand in 22/28nm, TSMC's
increasing order outflow opportunity, long-term opportunity in advanced packaging and photonics and that its niche
technology offerings should help it outperform its trailing-edge foundry peers. Our target price equates to 2026E/27E PB of

3.5x/3.2x.
Risks
Key downside risks to our target price include: 1) a longer-than-expected demand recovery; 2) more competition from peers in
28nm; 3) worse-than-expected developments from the company's China investment; 4) a significant decline in smartphone
end-demand; 5) poor contribution from Novatek's iPhone OLED business; and 6) fiercer ASP competition from Chinese peers.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

AI semi capex, in particular for compute chips, should outgrow
overall AI capex in 2028. We add cross-checks on ASICs after
AVGO’s guidance and the Qualcomm/AWS AI ASIC
announcement.
Will 2028 be another growth year for AI semis? Our US internet analyst Brian
Nowak published the Morgan Stanley AI Guidebook: Navigating the Age of
Inference, and suggests 12% CSP capex growth into 2028, raising investor questions
about AI semi growth momentum. Based on our latest supply chain checks, we

introduce preliminary 2028 CoWoS/CoPoS/EMIB-T capacity assumptions. In
aggregate, we still see 50% capacity growth in 2028 (see Exhibit 1), implying
flattish infrastructure (e.g., the shell and AI DC) spending and moderate memory
pricing in 2028.
Larger chip size and more applications (CPU, networking) to drive further
growth in 2028: All these packaging technologies are 2.5D (compute and memory
chips on side to side) for AI/HPC chips, including AI GPU, XPU, CPU, and networking.

•CoWoS (wafer based): We still see some CoW expansion at TSMC. For oS, TSMC
may need more partners than ASE. Our checks suggest both Amkor and Xintec
(non-covered) will diversify oS production in the US and Taiwan, respectively.
• CoPoS (panel-based): This is a panel-level process. After converting to 12-inch
CoWoS wafer equivalents, we assume 5–10kwpm in 2028. The initial target project
should be Nvidia’s Feynman Ultra GPU.
• EMIB-T (substrate-based): Although a substrate-based technology, we convert it

to 12-inch CoWoS wafer-equivalent capacity as well. One EMIB-T substrate can
generate 16 pcs of a 9x reticle-size chip, around 4x the chips a CoWoS wafer can
generate. Our checks indicate ~40k–45k wafer-equivalent EMIB-T capacity in 2028,
producing at least 2mn of Humufish (9x reticle) substrates. 40k–45k wafer
equivalents also imply 10-15% share in 2.5D packaging.
Read-across from recent ASIC guidance at Broadcom and the Qualcomm/AWS
partnership

•According to Joe Moore’s report: Broadcom Inc.: Earnings solid; raising FY 28 EPS,
more specific FY27 revenue guidance is now US$115 bn, and that could double again
in FY28. Our CoWoS supply-chain checks already see an AVGO AI lab customer
booking ~15k–30k CoWoS wafers for 2027.
•Qualcomm announced its ASIC partnership with AWS, a key Alchip ASIC customer.
However, the press release points to inference, different from Alchip’s Trainium4,
which covers both training and inference. We therefore see limited impact to Alchip.

TSMC CoWoS and CoPoS
With continual booming demand in AI, we expect TSMC and its OSAT partners to expedite
capacity expansion plans for CoWoS. We expect TSMC's CoWoS capacity to further build
to 260kwpm in 2028 from 130/200kwpm in 2026/2027, with 2028's expansion mainly

focusing in Arizona's AP9/10 and potentially in AP7. TSMC is now conducting trial
production for CoPoS in Taoyuan. As long as the progress goes well, we expect TSMC to
start building its CoPoS capacity, with the location also likely to be in AP9/10 or AP7P3.
We expect the non-TSMC camp to expand CoWoS capacity to 110kwpm by 2028 year-end
from 80kwpm by end-2027. For ASE/SPIL, we expect FoCoS+CoWoS capacity to rise from
30kwpm at 2027-end to 50-60kwpm at 2028-end, with expansion focused on CoWoS-L

and CoWoS-R. For Amkor, we expect CoWoS capacity to increase from 30kwpm at 2027-
end to 55-60kwpm at 2028-end, also focused on CoWoS-L and CoWoS-R.

For Intel, we see current average EMIB-M capacity being 110kwpm, which would slightly

to 15-20kwpm in 2027 and 40-45kwpm in 2028. All of the capacity mentioned above is
converted for  12-inch wafer equivalent, which we believe would be much more easier to

communicate and compared with TSMC CoWoS capacity.

consuming most of the capacities during 2027-28. We maintain our view that Intel EMIB-T
could still  produce close to 3mn units of Humufish from late 2027-2028, by assuming 4-5
chips per wafer of EMIB-T.

### Page 1

EQUITY: TECHNOLOGY
Panjit International   2481.TW 2481 TT
Global Markets Research
11 September 2026
Favorable pricing, product mix to elevate 2H26-2027F profit margins
New AI datacenter orders remain major growth driver
More positive on Panjit’s AI datacenter power MOSFET supply chain position 
Our recent market survey suggests sustained tight supply of select power discrete 
products in 2H26F, such as power/small signal MOSFET, and diodes. Future Electronics’ 
monthly report indicates lengthened lead times for many MOSFET and diode variants in 
Jul/Aug 2026, along with an uptrend in pricing (Fig 5). On the other hand, SDI’s (2351 TT, 
Buy) management indicated that IDM customers are placing more lead frame orders to the 
company with favorable pricing in 2H26E, in order to meet stronger AI-datacenter demand and 
to secure market share. As some products’ lead times have reached historical record levels 
(for e.g., select Schottky/switch diodes and LV/HV MOSFET lead times reached 52 weeks in 
Aug 2026, vs 20 weeks a year ago), and with limited capacity expansion among IDMs/ 
foundries in the near term, we expect the tight supply to continue in 2H26-1H27F. We also 
expect such a benign environment to be a tailwind for vendors to pass-through cost increases. 
We expect Panit’s 2H26-2027F revenue growth and margin expansion to sustain
Panjit’s 2Q26 revenue grew 16% q-q, better than management’s target, and was driven 
by improved demand across end markets. 2Q26 GM reached a 19-quarter high at 33.2% 
on a greater revenue scale, better product mix, and favorable pricing. We expect the 
revenue and profit margin q-q momentum to sustain in 2H26-2027F, as the company has 
secured more orders from the AI datacenter power discrete market, along with price hikes 
(mainly to pass-through rising fab manufacturing and material costs). We expect 3Q26-
4Q26F revenue to grow 10%/5% q-q, with AI datacenter related revenue contributing 12-14% 
total sales (vs 11% in 1H26). We also assume 2H26-2027F GM to reach 36.5%/37.3% (vs 
33.0% in 1H26) with higher AI and automotive sales exposure, better utilization rates across 
manufacturing sites, along with a third round of price hikes in 4Q26F. 
2026F/27F EPS raised by 3%/10%; TP increased to TWD214, implying 38.5% upside
We raise 2026F/27F EPS, as we assume contribution from more new AI datacenter 
orders mainly starting in 2H26-2027F, and expect a more favorable mix and pricing to 
form better margin profiles. Our TP of TWD214 is based on 25x 2027F EPS of TWD8.55 
(previous TP of TWD195 was based on 25x 2027F EPS of TWD7.79). The stock currently 
trades at 18x/16x 2027F/28F EPS.

### Page 3

Company profile
Panjit is a power semiconductor IDM headquartered in Taiwan. It currently manufactures and sells power discrete (including diodes, MOSFET, and
SIC), Power IC, and solar products. The company’s products are widely used in many end applications including industrial, green energy, consumer
electronics, automotive, computers, power supply, and communication.
Valuation Methodology
Our TP of TWD214 is based on 25x 2027F EPS of TWD8.55. We use 25x to derive our TP, vs historical P/E range of 18x since 2018 (The stock

traded in a range from 15-33x when the company was in earnings growth upcycle). The benchmark to the stock is TAIEX.
Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price
Downside risks: 1) global macroeconomic uncertainty that may drag demand for the company's products, especially auto and industrial; 2) slower-
than-expected supply chain inventory destocking; and 3) pricing competition from peers if global demand is worse than expected.
ESG

Panjit requires itself to uphold the business principles of “innovation, growth, responsibility, and sustainability” in the global semiconductor supply
chain in the face of unprecedented changes in the aspects of global environment and climate, economy and society. The company actively
promotes and continues to make improvement in environmental protection, employee safety and health, labor conditions, moral values, and the
maintenance of energy, striving to become a member of the green enterprises in the world while constantly strengthening ESG (the beauty of the

Environment, the goodness in society, and the truthfulness in governance) actions to respond to changes and challenges in the future with a high
level of dynamics.

Definition of Nomura Group's equity research rating system and sectors
The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, 
subject to limited management discretion. An analyst’s target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an 
appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow 
analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated 
target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.

SECTORS
A 'Bullish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to outperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Neutral' stance, 
indicates that the analyst expects the sector to perform in line with the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Bearish' stance, indicates that 
the analyst expects the sector to underperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. Sectors that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 
'N/A' are not assigned ratings. Benchmarks are as follows: United States: S&P 500; Europe: Dow Jones STOXX 600; Global Emerging 
Markets (ex-Asia): MSCI Emerging Markets ex-Asia. Japan/Asia ex-Japan: Sector ratings are not assigned.

Target Price
A Target Price, if discussed, indicates the analyst’s forecast for the share price with a 12-month time horizon, reflecting in part the analyst's 
estimates for the company's earnings. The achievement of any target price may be impeded by general market and macroeconomic trends, and 
by other risks related to the company or the market, and may not occur if the company's earnings differ from estimates.

EQUITY: TECHNOLOGY
SDI Corporation   2351.TW 2351 TT
Global Markets Research
11 September 2026
Stronger power lead frame outlook in 2H26-2027F
Heat spreader products the cherry on top; maintain Buy
We see further 2026/27F growth potential from power lead frame and heat spreader
Our recent industry channel checks suggests: 1) stronger power lead frame demand, 
especially from AI datacenter related in 2H26-2027F: As mentioned in our previous note, 
global integrated device manufacturers’ (IDM) 3Q26E sales outlook continues to show strength 
(3Q26E weighted average revenue y-y of +17% / q-q of +7%, vs +18% / +11% in 2Q26; this 
implies the fifth quarter of y-y expansion since 3Q25). Specifically, a few of SDI’s key IDM 
customers at their 2Q26 earnings calls raised 2026-27E AI datacenter revenue with stronger 
demand and faster capacity expansion (two customers’ 2027E-related sales should double y-y, 
according to our channel checks). We expect SDI’s 2027F power lead frame revenue from AI-
related field to realize 134% y-y growth (15% of total sales vs 8% in 2026F), with 60 ongoing 
projects currently; and 2) favorable pricing and product mix leading to better 2026/27F 
margin profile: Given supply tightness across several end markets, we expect further pricing 
improvement for SDI in 2H26F, after two rounds of price hikes in 1H26. In addition, given 
stronger demand from auto and AI datacenter (with GM better than other end markets), we 
expect SDI’s 2H26F/FY27F GM to reach 22.1%/23.0% vs 20.0% in 1H26.
2026-27F to mark the milestone of heat spreader business development
In addition to continued capacity expansion for power lead frame products, SDI’s management has 
decided to add more stamping equipment (ranging from 100-ton, 200-ton, to500-ton) in 2026-27E 
to handle increasing demand for its newly-developed product – heat spreader (including hat, cavity, 
ring/stiffener, and micro-channel lid, or MCL). The company will focus on automotive, ASIC/CPU, 
and networking in AI datacenter fields. Given superior manufacturing capability (20-30µ coplanarity 
vs 50-70µ of industrial average), it has secured four major orders from OSAT, auto, and IC design 
customers, with management expecting major revenue contribution from 2027E (we estimate 
3%/7% of 2027/28F total sales). We believe there can be sales and earnings contribution upside 
once we are able to confirm more order receiving from higher-end products.  
Raise 2026/27F EPS assumptions by 8%/17%; TP raised to TWD327
We raise 2026/27F sales and earnings growth (Fig. 1) with stronger order placing from global 
IDM customers, along with initial revenue contribution from heat spreader products. Our new TP 
of TWD327 is based on an unchanged multiple of 28x 2027F EPS of TWD11.68 (previously 28x 
2H26-1H27F EPS of TWD8.96), vs SDI’s historical average of 22.5x since 2015 (a range of 5.6x 
to 70.6x). The stock currently trades at 20x/16x 2027/28F EPS.

Company profile
SDI is a leading global semiconductor lead frame supplier headquartered in Taiwan. The company is the largest power semiconductor lead frame
manufacturer in the world, with its primary focus on automotive, industrial and AI applications.
Valuation Methodology
Our target price of TWD327 is based on 28x 2027F EPS of TWD11.68 vs historical average of 22.5x since 2015 with a range of 5.6x to 70.6x. The
benchmark for is this stock is TAIEX.

Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price
Downside risks: 1) slower-than-expected auto, industrial, and consumer electronic demand recovery, 2) delays of new products' mass production, 3)
pricing competition from global peers, and 4) dramatic copper price drop in short periods, which should be a negative impact on SDI's near-term GM.

Definition of Nomura Group's equity research rating system and sectors
The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, 
subject to limited management discretion. An analyst’s target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an 
appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow 
analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated 
target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.

SECTORS
A 'Bullish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to outperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Neutral' stance, 
indicates that the analyst expects the sector to perform in line with the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Bearish' stance, indicates that 
the analyst expects the sector to underperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. Sectors that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 
'N/A' are not assigned ratings. Benchmarks are as follows: United States: S&P 500; Europe: Dow Jones STOXX 600; Global Emerging 
Markets (ex-Asia): MSCI Emerging Markets ex-Asia. Japan/Asia ex-Japan: Sector ratings are not assigned.

Target Price
A Target Price, if discussed, indicates the analyst’s forecast for the share price with a 12-month time horizon, reflecting in part the analyst's 
estimates for the company's earnings. The achievement of any target price may be impeded by general market and macroeconomic trends, and 
by other risks related to the company or the market, and may not occur if the company's earnings differ from estimates.

AI’s Hidden Backbone
We view this as a selective, specification-driven materials cycle
rather than a broad commodity upturn. The strongest
positioning belongs to suppliers with next-generation
qualifications, reliable manufacturing yields, and access to
constrained upstream inputs.

Greater China Technology Hardware
Asia Pacific
Industry View In-Line
AI-driven specification upgrades are reshaping the economics of copper-clad
laminate (CCL), the core material in PCBs, and driving demand for higher-

performance copper foil and glass cloth. We expect the global CCL TAM to rise
from US$19B in 2025 to US$47B by 2030, implying a 20% CAGR (vs market
expectations at US$35-40B), with AI/data-center applications accounting for 90%
of incremental growth and nearly two-thirds of demand by decade-end.
Content, not units, is the key growth driver. We estimate rising material intensity
accounts for 84% of AI-related CCL growth, as next-generation compute and

networking platforms move to higher-layer-count PCBs, lower-loss CCL and
smoother HVLP copper foil. Our bottom-up model implies the HVLP4 market
grows from <US$50M in 2025 to US$2.8B by 2030, a 123% CAGR. Extending the
same framework further downstream, we forecast the global PCB TAM will rise
from US$58bn to US$135bn over 2025–30, an 18% CAGR.
Broadening the AI trade upstream. We think high-end CCL, HVLP copper foil and
advanced glass cloth have entered an earnings upcycle but have yet to reach full

earnings realization and peak-cycle conditions. AI-driven specification upgrades are
reducing the number of  qualified suppliers and supporting mix, pricing and margins,
while long qualification cycles, lower yields and equipment bottlenecks should slow
the supply response.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with
companies covered in Morgan Stanley Research. As a result,
investors should be aware that the firm may have a conflict of
interest that could affect the objectivity of Morgan Stanley

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
Long qualification cycles and lower production yields in advanced copper foil and
glass cloth should keep effective high-end CCL supply tight into 2028.
Our proprietary bottom-up analysis quantifies copper foil, CCL and PCB content
across Nvidia, AMD, TPU and Trainium platforms.
We introduce a scorecard comparing 16 PCB, substrate & materials suppliers on

six factors to distinguish structural winners from cyclical beneficiaries.
DDR4-like supply squeeze; standard E-glass pricing likely has further upside as
capacity shifts toward higher-value, more advanced grade cloth.
Initiate at OW on EMC (NT$8,400 PT), TUC (NT$2,700 PT), Co-Tech (NT$730
PT), and KB Laminates (HK$75 PT).

Executive Summary
Why read this report?
We provide a comprehensive understanding of what copper foil, and copper-clad
laminates are and how they fit into the PCB supply chain. In addition, we have built
a proprietary bottom-up model to model out the copper foil and copper-clad
laminates market (please reach out to us for the model).
We also broke down the copper foil, copper-clad laminate, and printed circuit
board content per AI system across the different Nvidia, AMD, TPU, and Trainium

architectures.
AI has completely overhauled the PCB supply chain, going all the way up to upstream
materials like CCL (key raw material used in PCB production), copper foil (used in CCL
production), as well as electronic glass cloth (used in CCL production) and others. ABF
substrates are also seeing similar tailwinds, but we have talked about that here, here, and
here. In this report, we focus primarily on CCL and copper foil, but also touch on glass

cloth.
We forecast the CCL market to grow at a 20% CAGR over 2025-30, to US$47B from
US$19B (2.5x). Unit and content growth both contribute. AI data center cluster
deployments lift volumes, while faster signal transmission speeds require upgraded CCL
to contain insertion loss and crosstalk, on top of a mix shift toward higher layer-count and
more complex PCBs.
Against this demand, we see high-end CCL as under-supplied. Only a handful of suppliers

globally are qualified for M8+ grades, including EMC, Panasonic, TUC, Doosan, and
Shengyi. Because CCL capacity is grade-agnostic in architecture, nameplate capacity
overstates effective high-grade supply, and M7/M8+ supply-demand is therefore difficult
to quantify with precision. The absence of a precise gap does not change the direction. We
expect high-end tightness to translate into firmer pricing and margin expansion for the
qualified incumbents.

In copper foil, we forecast the high-end HVLP4 market to reach US$2.8B by 2030, a
123% CAGR over 2025-2030, though off a de minimis base. HVLP4 (hyper very low
profile) foil is the enabling input for low-loss, high-speed CCL, and therefore a gating item
in the AI PCB supply chain.
Effective capacity rests with five suppliers today: Mitsui Kinzoku, Co-Tech, Furukawa,
Fukuda and Copper Foil Luxembourg at roughly 1,000t/month, with Mitsui alone at 41%

of 2026 capacity. Adding to that base is harder than nameplate suggests. Converting
HVLP2 lines is not one-for-one; the longer production cycle cuts effective output by  more
than 40%. New lines require 6-12 months to ramp, and sit behind delivery queues for
surface-treatment equipment concentrated among a small number of Japanese suppliers.
We model demand rising to 39.2kt in 2027 from 12.3kt in 2026 (+218% y/y), and further
growing to 52.0kt in 2028 (+33% y/y). That would leave the market in a deficit of 31% by

### Page 5

M
Foundation
Morgan Stanley Research 5
2027 and 20% by 2028. As such, we expect a handful of qualified producers to hold
meaningful pricing power over that window.
Our conclusion is that CCL makers that are able to secure the full input set of cloth, foil
and resin should hold pricing power over downstream customers.
As a result of our bottom-up analysis of CCL and its upstream materials, we expect the
PCB TAM to grow from US$58B in 2025 to US$135B by 2030, representing an 18%

CAGR.
Beyond discovery: Why high-end CCL stocks still have room
to run
We believe the market continues to underestimate the extent to which AI
infrastructure investment will expand end demand for copper-clad laminate. Our 2030
CCL total addressable market estimate of US$47B is meaningfully above market forecasts
of US$35-40B.
The key difference lies not only in our assumptions for AI server and data-center unit
growth, but also in the increasing material intensity of next-generation computing and

networking platforms. Higher layer counts, larger and more complex PCBs, faster data-
transmission requirements, and the growing use of premium low-loss and high-speed
materials should drive CCL content per system materially higher. This is all made possible
with more advanced copper foil  with tighter surface-profile, signal-integrity, and reliability
requirements.
Structural demand is supported by capex. The spending backdrop still has more than a

year of visible growth in it. Our  house view on cash cloud capex now stands at US$1.2T in
2026 (+104% y/y) and US$1.6T  in 2027 (+38% y/y) vs. consensus at US$1.39T for 2027.
This compares with buyside expectations of US$1.8T+ (including financial and operating
leases), suggesting there could still be meaningful room for further upward consensus
revisions.
CCL content is growing faster than AI-system units. The demand driver is a specification
ladder, not a single product cycle, and that distinction is what makes the cycle durable.

Layer counts on AI server motherboards are increasing with each generation to support
additional routing space for more signals as AI boards become more complex, while rising
signal and thermal demands also support the adoption of higher grade CCLs. Crucially,
each rung multiplies rather than adds, because moving up a grade changes the resin
chemistry, the copper-foil profile and the glass-cloth grade simultaneously. Content per
rack can therefore keep rising even if unit shipment growth moderates. The continuing

migration toward lower-loss grades is another reason the earnings opportunity may have
further to run.

The real scarcity is qualified, high-yield capacity. High-speed laminate is not a
commodity that can be replaced solely on price; materials must be validated for signal

loss, thermal reliability, dimensional stability and compatibility with specific PCB
fabrication processes. For example, an upgrade to M8 grade CCL is not a simple
incremental upgrade from M7. It requires simultaneous improvements in low-loss resin,
smoother HVLP copper foil, higher-spec low-Dk glass cloth, and much tighter
manufacturing tolerances. These changes narrow the process window, reduce throughput
and yields, and increase scrap, inspection, and qualification costs. At the same time, the

pool of suppliers able to produce M8 reliably at scale is much smaller, while AI-server
demand is accelerating, creating significantly tighter effective supply. That is why the M8
CCL ASP is more than double that of M7 grade CCL (Exhibit 9).
Once a material has been designed into a high-volume platform, changing it can require
renewed signal-integrity work, reliability testing and PCB-process validation. That creates
design-in persistence, and we believe a supplier’s qualification at M9 (for example) should

be viewed as more than a one-generation design win; it creates a cumulative advantage for
the next material transition. By the time a CCL supplier is qualified for M9, it has already
demonstrated that it can meet demanding electrical, thermal, dimensional-stability, and
manufacturability requirements at commercial scale. It has also accumulated valuable
process data, refined production yields, and developed working relationships with the end
customer, PCB fabricators, and upstream material suppliers. When the end customer

begins evaluating M10 or higher-grade materials, the incumbent can build from a proven
technical and manufacturing base rather than starting the qualification process from
scratch.
This advantage is reinforced by earlier access to customer roadmaps and opportunities for
joint development. A qualified M9 supplier is more likely to understand the customer’s
next-generation loss budget, stack-up constraints, reliability requirements, and production
timeline, allowing it to tailor its M10 product before broader qualification begins.

Customers also have an incentive to work with proven suppliers because changing
materials can require renewed signal-integrity modeling, PCB-process adjustments,

### Page 7

M
Foundation
Morgan Stanley Research 7
reliability testing, and yield validation. M9 qualification therefore does not guarantee
success at M10, as each generation can reopen competition, but it meaningfully improves
the probability of qualification, shortens time to market, and creates a compounding
technological and commercial lead.

Where are we in the cycle?
In our cycle framework, we place high-end CCL and HVLP copper foil at past the trough,
but still ahead of full earnings realization and peak-cycle conditions. Demand is being

driven by a multi-year migration toward higher layer-count PCBs and lower-loss materials,
while qualified supply remains constrained by long customer qualification cycles, lower
yields and upstream bottlenecks. We therefore expect mix, pricing and margins to improve
through 2027-28; however, the opportunity remains selective, as commodity-grade CCL
can stay oversupplied even as qualified high-end materials tighten, making this a stock-
selection cycle rather than a broad sector call.

Conclusion
We view the current demand cycle as being driven by a sustained rise in material
specifications rather than by a single product refresh. This distinction is important, as it
suggests the opportunity could be more structural and durable than previous electronics
cycles, which were often more dependent on unit shipments and shorter replacement
cycles.
In our view, the specification upgrades are also multiplicative rather than merely additive.

Moving to a higher-performance grade CCL typically requires simultaneous changes across
the material stack, involving more advanced resin systems, lower-profile copper foil, and
higher-grade glass cloth. At the same time, increasingly complex AI server and networking
architectures require PCBs with more layers, greater routing density, tighter signal-
integrity tolerances, and, in some cases, larger board dimensions. As a result, the value of
CCL, copper foil, and related materials used per system, or per rack, can continue to

increase even if the pace of server or rack shipment growth begins to moderate.
The main drivers of this content growth include:
• Migration toward higher-grade CCL. Rising data-transfer speeds, higher operating
frequencies, and greater thermal loads are increasing the need for low-loss, high-
speed CCL materials. As AI accelerators and networking systems move to faster
interconnect standards, electrical performance becomes increasingly sensitive to

dielectric loss, signal attenuation, and material consistency. This should support a
continued mix shift toward higher-grade CCLs with more advanced resin
formulations and tighter manufacturing requirements.
• Increasing PCB layer counts. AI servers, accelerator boards, and high-speed
switches require substantially more routing capacity to support a growing number
of processors, memory modules, power-delivery components, and high-speed
input/output channels. Higher layer counts allow designers to accommodate this

complexity while maintaining signal and power integrity. This increases the amount
of CCL and copper foil required per board and can also raise manufacturing
complexity and average selling prices.
Taken together, the continued migration toward higher-layer-count PCBs, lower-loss and
higher-speed CCL, more advanced copper foil, and potentially larger board formats should
support sustained growth in material content per system. We believe this specification-

driven upgrade cycle creates further revenue and earnings upside for the broader CCL and
copper-foil supply chain, particularly for suppliers that are already qualified on leading AI
server, accelerator, and networking platforms. This underappreciated content opportunity
is central to our positive industry view.

Stock implications
Elite Materials Co. (2383.TW, OW, PT NT$8,400)
EMC is a global leader in high-speed, low-loss CCL, with dominant market share across all

major GPU and ASIC customer platforms. It continues to invest for future growth, with
capacity expected to grow from 5,850k sheets/month at the end of 2025 to 11,250k
sheets/month by the end of 2028, or 92% growth. Most of these capacity additions will
be to support advanced grade CCL demand (M8+) over the next few years, driven by rising
demand for AI-related systems. We therefore forecast EMC's revenue to grow at a 76%
CAGR in 2025-2028, but we expect net profit to grow at a faster rate of 117% over the

same period. On EPS, our forecasts for 2026-28 are NT$122.17, NT$266.24, and NT
$416.24, respectively.
Price target and valuation discussion: Our price target of NT$8,400 implies 20x CY28 P/
E or 0.36x PEG, which we think is fair vs. its three year average of 14x because of the
strong revenue and profit outlook driven by higher grade CCLs. In the higher grade CCL
segment, there are also less capable suppliers, so competition decreases.
The 20x CY28 P/E implied by our price target is slightly above the past 3Y average +1SD

of 19x, but much lower than the 32x recent P/E peak. We deem this valuation as fair,
because EMC is benefitting from an earnings growth cycle fueled by stronger AI server
CCL demand, EMC's own mix improvement and continued pricing adjustments, which
supports margin expansion from 29.8% in 2025 to 41.4% by 2028 and an EPS CAGR of
117% over 2025-2028, on our estimates. Our 20x CY28 P/E for EMC is also higher than our

### Page 11

17x CY28 P/E for TUC, reflecting EMC’s leading position in the AI CCL market in terms of
both technology capabilities and production capacity. The stock is trading at just 12.8x
CY28 P/E, below EMC's past 3Y average of 14x and Shengyi's current valuation of 21x
CY28 P/E. Thus, we view the risk reward as attractive.
Taiwan Union Co. (6274.TWO, OW, PT NT$2,700)
TUC is another leading supplier of high-speed, low-loss CCL in Taiwan, though behind

EMC, with particular strength in high-end networking switches at 400G, 800G and above,
as well as growing exposure to AI ASIC platforms, including AWS Trainium from Trainium2
onward. Its M7+ mix is expected to rise from approximately 36% of sales in 2025 to 46%
in 2028, while capacity grows from 2,300K sheets/month at the end of 2025 to 5,300K
sheets/month by the end of 2028, an increase of approximately 130%. The richer product
mix and pricing adjustments should support gross-margin expansion from 22.7% in 2025

to 36.0% in 2028. Our forecasts for 2026-28 EPS are NT$40.17, NT$94.43 and NT$156.68,
respectively, implying a 138% CAGR over 2025-2028.
Price target and valuation discussion: Our NT$2,700 price target implies 17x CY28 P/E,
or 0.26x PEG, vs. TUC’s three-year average of 13x. We think this premium is fair given the
rapid M7+ mix shift, capacity expansion and margin uplift, together with TUC’s strong
networking franchise and growing hyperscaler exposure. Its position as the primary, if not

sole, supplier of thick-copper CCL used by a leading data-center power-solution provider
offers an additional differentiated growth and pricing lever.
The 17x CY28 P/E implied by our price target is in line with the past 3Y average +1SD of
17x. We deem this valuation as fair, because TUC is benefitting from an earnings growth
cycle fueled by stronger AI server/networking CCL demand, TUC's own mix improvement
and continued pricing adjustments, which supports margin expansion from 22.7% in 2025

to 36.0% by 2028 and an EPS CAGR of 138% over 2025-2028, on our estimates. The stock
is trading at just 8.6x CY28 P/E, below the past 3Y average -1SD of 9.4x. Thus, we view  risk
reward as attractive.
Co-Tech (8358.TWO, OW, PT NT$730).
Co-Tech is the leading advanced  copper foil company in Taiwan and one of the few
qualified suppliers of advanced RTF and HVLP3/4 copper foil and is emerging as the most
important second source to Mitsui for AI servers and high-end networking. The company

stopped supplying conventional HTE and standard RTF in 3Q26, redirecting its capacity
toward higher-value RG and HVLP products, while its HVLP4 officially entered  the Nvidia
supply chain in 2025 and ramped up mass production in 2026. We model Co-Tech’s
HVLP4 capacity increasing from less than 50 tonnes/month in 2025 to approximately 200
tonnes at the end of 2026, 700 tonnes at the end of 2027 and 800 tonnes at the end of
2028. This would increase its global capacity share from approximately 13% in 2026 to

21% in 2028, making it the second-largest supplier after Mitsui. Our forecasts for 2026-28
EPS are NT$9.34, NT$18.59 and NT$31.63, respectively, implying a 96% CAGR over 2025-
28.
Price target and valuation discussion: Our NT$730 price target implies 23x CY28 P/E, or
0.33x PEG, vs. Co-Tech's three-year average of 20x. We think the premium is fair given Co-
Tech’s qualification moat, rapid capacity ramp and exposure to a structurally under-

Kingboard Laminates (1888.HK, OW, PT: HK$75).
KB Laminates is the world’s largest CCL producer by volume and is differentiated by its
vertical integration across copper foil, glass yarn and cloth, epoxy resin and paper-based
materials, providing advantages in cost, supply security and production planning. Although
its current product mix remains weighted toward commodity FR-4, with less than 5% of
capacity allocated to M6+ products, KB is moving up the specification curve. Its first 350K

sheets/month of M6+ capacity is scheduled to come online in 1H27, followed by another
350K sheets/month in 1H28, while a new 21,000-tonne high-frequency and low-loss
copper-foil plant is expected to start production in mid-2027. We forecast FY25-28
revenue to grow at a 42% CAGR and net profit at a faster 91% CAGR. Our FY26-28 EPS
forecasts are HK$2.73, HK$4.51 and HK$5.40, respectively.
Price target and valuation discussion: Our HK$75 price target implies 14x CY28 P/E, or

0.7x PEG, modestly above its three-year average of 12.8x. We think this is fair given the
profit-growth outlook, the cost and supply-security benefits of vertical integration, and
the earnings optionality from its M6+ expansion. However, KB should trade at a lower
multiple than the leading high-end CCL suppliers until advanced grades become a
meaningfully larger part of its mix, as commodity FR-4 remains its core market and its
high-end qualification position is still at an earlier stage.

The 14x CY28 P/E implied by our price target is slightly above the past 3Y average of
12.8x. We deem this valuation as fair, because KB Laminates is benefitting from an
earnings growth cycle fueled by price hikes of its FR4 CCLs and glass cloth, as well as its
gradual penetration into the higher-end CCL material market, which supports margin
expansion from 19.6% in 2025 to 41.7% by 2028 and an EPS CAGR of 91% over 2025
2028, on our estimates. That said, we believe the company remains more of a cyclical play

compared to its Taiwanese peers including EMC and TUC. Thus, we view the 1x re-rating
vs. its past 3Y P/E average as fair. The stock is trading at just 8.5x CY28 P/E, below its past
3Y average of 12.8x. Therefore, we view risk reward as attractive.

What are the key risks? 
• A slowdown in AI infrastructure investment over the next several years. 
Demand for high-end copper foil and copper-clad laminate is increasingly tied to AI 
servers, networking equipment, and data-center expansion. A moderation in 
hyperscaler capital spending, slower growth in AI workloads, or longer server 
replacement cycles could weaken demand and delay expected capacity utilization.
• Company-specific execution or yield challenges. Lower-than-expected yields 
could result in higher unit costs and a slower margin recovery. This may create a 
gap between reported profitability and market expectations, particularly during 
the qualification and initial mass-production stages.
• Failure to qualify for next-generation materials platforms. Suppliers must 
typically undergo customer qualification processes before their products can be 
used in new server, switch, and accelerator platforms. An inability to meet 
increasingly stringent requirements for signal integrity, thermal performance, 
dimensional stability, or reliability could cause a supplier to miss an entire product 
cycle and lose share in higher-margin applications.
• Competition from Chinese suppliers. Continued investment by Chinese copper 
foil and CCL manufacturers could increase competition in higher-grade segments. 
• Constraints in upstream raw-material supply. Shortages in materials such as 
glass cloth, specialty resin, and copper foil could limit production volumes. 
• Faster-than-expected adoption of co-packaged optics. A more rapid transition to 
co-packaged optics could shorten electrical signal paths and reduce the need for 
certain high-speed PCB interconnections within networking equipment, resulting in 
a downgrade of CCL material used, therefore reducing some content opportunity 
of premium low-loss CCL and copper foil.
• Copper price changes. In estimating the TAM for copper foil and CCL, we have not 
assumed any specific movement in copper prices over the next few years. Instead, 
we have held copper prices constant at current levels.

AI-Related Demand Will Add Over US$70B to the PCB
Market
We estimate the global PCB addressable market will grow at an 18% CAGR between
2025 and 2030, increasing from US$58B to US$135B. This expansion will be driven
overwhelmingly by demand from AI and data-center infrastructure. As shown in Exhibit
22, the AI and data center-related PCB market is expected to rise from US$13B in 2025 to
US$86B by 2030, more than a sixfold increase. Its share of total PCB industry revenue

would therefore increase from roughly 20-25% in 2025 to 64% by the end of the decade.
On these assumptions, AI and data-center applications account for essentially all of the
industry’s net growth over the period, while demand across the remaining end markets is
broadly stable.
The opportunity is also expected to be diversified across end segments. Growth should
extend across PCBs used in general servers, GPU servers, custom ASIC servers,
networking switches, and optical modules as demand continues to grow across the board

and computing clusters continue to scale and grow. In addition to higher shipment
volumes, these applications carry significantly greater PCB content per system, reflecting
larger board sizes (potentially), higher layer counts, more advanced materials, tighter
electrical requirements, and more complex manufacturing processes. The combination of
volume growth and rising PCB value per system underpins the sharp expansion expected
in the AI and data-center segment through 2030.
